events.label: Scanlan says the order is flourishing and asks why McMurdo left Chicago

communicates.speaker: scanlan_lodge_341_vermissa_valley
communicates.content: Well, there are plenty of us about. You won’t find the order more flourishing anywhere in the States than right here in Vermissa Valley. But we could do with some lads like you. I can’t understand a spry man of the union finding no work to do in Chicago. Then why did you leave?

events.label: McMurdo nods toward the policemen and implies they would be glad to know the reason for his departure

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I guess those chaps would be glad to know.

events.label: Scanlan asks whether McMurdo is in trouble and whether it is a penitentiary job or a killing

communicates.speaker: scanlan_lodge_341_vermissa_valley
communicates.content: In trouble? A penitentiary job? Not a killing!

events.label: McMurdo rebukes Scanlan for asking and says it is too early to speak of such things

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: It’s early days to talk of such things. I’ve my own good reasons for leaving Chicago, and let that be enough for you. Who are you that you should take it on yourself to ask such things?

events.label: Scanlan asks McMurdo where he is bound for and where he is staying

communicates.speaker: scanlan_lodge_341_vermissa_valley
communicates.content: Where are you bound for now? Where are you staying?

events.label: McMurdo shows an envelope and gives an address

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Here is the address—Jacob Shafter, Sheridan Street. It’s a boarding house that was recommended by a man I knew in Chicago.

events.label: The policeman gives McMurdo advice about Vermissa and Boss McGinty

communicates.speaker: local_police_sergeant
communicates.content: Vermissa is out of my beat. I live at Hobson’s Patch, and that’s here where we are drawing up. If you’re in trouble in Vermissa, go straight to the Union House and see Boss McGinty. He is the Bodymaster of Vermissa Lodge, and nothing can happen in these parts unless Black Jack McGinty wants it. Maybe we’ll meet in lodge one of these evenings. But mind my words: If you are in trouble, go to Boss McGinty.

events.label: Scanlan descends from the carriage
McMurdo remains in the carriage as night falls and the train moves through the furnace district
A policeman remarks on the appearance of the fiery district

communicates.speaker: local_police_sergeant
communicates.content: I guess hell must look something like that. For that matter, I allow that hell must be something like that. If there are worse devils down yonder than some we could name, it’s more than I’d expect. I guess you are new to this part, young man?

events.label: McMurdo answers the policeman rudely

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, what if I am? What the hell is it to you who are my friends? Did I ask you for your advice, or did you think me such a sucker that I couldn’t move without it? You speak when you are spoken to, and by the Lord you’d have to wait a long time if it was me!

events.label: The policemen react to McMurdo’s hostility

communicates.speaker: local_police_sergeant
communicates.content: No offense, stranger. It was a warning for your own good, seeing that you are, by your own showing, new to the place. Maybe we’ll see more of you before very long. You’re a real hand-picked one, if I am a judge. I guess we may meet again.

events.label: McMurdo declares his name and where he can be found

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’m not afraid of you, and don’t you think it! My name’s Jack McMurdo—see? If you want me, you’ll find me at Jacob Shafter’s on Sheridan Street, Vermissa; so I’m not hiding from you, am I? Day or night I dare to look the like of you in the face—don’t make any mistake about that!

events.label: The train arrives at the ill-lit station and the passengers clear off the platform.
McMurdo picks up his gripsack and starts to leave the platform.
A miner accosts McMurdo and offers to carry his grip and show him the road.

communicates.speaker: young_irishman
communicates.content: By Gar, mate! you know how to speak to the cops. It was grand to hear you. Let me carry your grip and show you the road. I’m passing Shafter’s on the way to my own shack.

events.label: The miners give McMurdo friendly good-nights as they leave the platform.

communicates.speaker: miners
communicates.content: Good-nights

events.label: McMurdo becomes a notable figure in Vermissa before setting foot in the town.
McMurdo and the miner walk through Vermissa toward the centre of town.
The miner identifies the Union House, names Jack McGinty as the boss there, and warns McMurdo about the Scowrers and McGinty.

communicates.speaker: young_irishman
communicates.content: That’s the Union House. Jack McGinty is the boss there. I thought his name was known clear across the country. It’s been in the papers often enough. There’s only one set of affairs that you’ll hear of in these parts, and that’s the affairs of the Scowrers. Man, you won’t live long in these parts if you speak in the open street like that. Many a man has had the life beaten out of him for less. If killing is murder, then God knows there is murder and to spare. Don’t you dare to breathe the name of Jack McGinty in connection with it, stranger; for every whisper goes back to him, and he is not one that is likely to let it pass. Now, that’s the house you’re after, that one standing back from the street. You’ll find old Jacob Shafter that runs it as honest a man as lives in this township.

events.label: McMurdo reaches Shafter's house and knocks at the door
Ettie Shafter opens the door
Ettie Shafter speaks to McMurdo about expecting her father back

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: I thought it was father. Did you come to see him? He is down town. I expect him back every minute.

events.label: McMurdo speaks to Ettie Shafter about board

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: No, miss. I’m in no hurry to see him. But your house was recommended to me for board. I thought it might suit me—and now I know it will.

events.label: Ettie Shafter invites McMurdo inside and introduces herself

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Come right in, sir. I’m Miss Ettie Shafter, Mr. Shafter’s daughter. My mother’s dead, and I run the house. You can sit down by the stove in the front room until father comes along—Ah, here he is! So you can fix things with him right away.

events.label: Mr. Shafter arrives at the house
McMurdo explains his business to Mr. Shafter and gives his Chicago referral chain

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: A man named Murphy gave me the address in Chicago. He in turn had had it from someone else.

events.label: Mr. Shafter agrees to board McMurdo for seven dollars a week in advance
McMurdo takes up board and lodging at Shafter's house
McMurdo becomes prominent among the boarders
The young Irishman openly admires the daughter of the house and wins her heart
The young Irishman tells Ettie that he loves her and keeps repeating it despite discouragement

communicates.speaker: young_irishman
communicates.content: I love you.

events.label: The young Irishman responds to the idea of someone else and says Ettie will eventually say yes

communicates.speaker: young_irishman
communicates.content: Someone else? Well, the worse luck for someone else! Let him look out for himself! Am I to lose my life’s chance and all my heart’s desire for someone else? You can keep on saying no, Ettie: the day will come when you will say yes, and I’m young enough to wait.

events.label: The young Irishman speaks charmingly and with mystery to Ettie
McMurdo gets a temporary job as a bookkeeper
McMurdo does not yet report himself to the lodge head
Mike Scanlan visits McMurdo and asks why he has not reported to the Bodymaster

communicates.speaker: scanlan_lodge_341_vermissa_valley
communicates.content: Say, McMurdo, I remembered your address, so I made bold to call. I’m surprised that you’ve not reported to the Bodymaster. Why haven’t you seen Boss McGinty yet?

events.label: McMurdo says he had to find a job and has been busy

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, I had to find a job. I have been busy.

events.label: Scanlan warns McMurdo to make time for the Bodymaster and to avoid running against him

communicates.speaker: scanlan_lodge_341_vermissa_valley
communicates.content: You must find time for him if you have none for anything else. Good Lord, man! you’re a fool not to have been down to the Union House and registered your name the first morning after you came here! If you run against him—well, you mustn’t, that’s all!

events.label: McMurdo says he has been a lodge member for over two years and that duties were not so pressing in Chicago

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’ve been a member of the lodge for over two years, Scanlan, but I never heard that duties were so pressing as all that. Well, it’s the same society here.

events.label: Scanlan questions McMurdo and looks at him fixedly

communicates.speaker: scanlan_lodge_341_vermissa_valley
communicates.content: Is it? Isn’t it? You’ll tell me that in a month’s time.

events.label: Scanlan says he heard McMurdo talked with the patrolmen after leaving the train

communicates.speaker: scanlan_lodge_341_vermissa_valley
communicates.content: I hear you had a talk with the patrolmen after I left the train. Oh, it got about—things do get about for good and for bad in this district.

events.label: Scanlan laughs and urges McMurdo to visit Shafter at once

communicates.speaker: scanlan_lodge_341_vermissa_valley
communicates.content: You go and see him, my lad. It’s not the police but you that he’ll hate if you don’t. Now, take a friend’s advice and go at once!

events.label: McMurdo meets Shafter in Shafter's private room and they speak about Ettie

communicates.speaker: jake_shafter
communicates.content: It seems to me, mister, that you are gettin’ set on my Ettie. Ain’t that so, or am I wrong? Vell, I vant to tell you right now that it ain’t no manner of use. There’s someone slipped in afore you. Vell, you can lay that she told you truth. But did she tell you who it vas? I dare say not, the leetle baggage! Perhaps she did not vish to frighten you avay.

events.label: McMurdo admits his interest in Ettie

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Yes, that is so.

events.label: Shafter names Teddy Baldwin as the rival for Ettie

communicates.speaker: jake_shafter
communicates.content: It is Teddy Baldwin.

events.label: McMurdo asks who Teddy Baldwin is and Shafter explains that he is a boss of the Scowrers

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: And who the devil is he?

events.label: McMurdo asks what the Scowrers are and Shafter identifies them as the Eminent Order of Freemen

communicates.speaker: jake_shafter
communicates.content: The Scowrers are the Eminent Order of Freemen!

events.label: McMurdo states that he is a member of the order

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Why, I am a member of that order myself.

events.label: Shafter says he would not have kept McMurdo in his house if he had known he was in the order

communicates.speaker: jake_shafter
communicates.content: I vould never have had you in my house if I had known it—not if you vere to pay me a hundred dollar a veek.

events.label: McMurdo defends the order as one for charity and good fellowship

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: What’s wrong with the order? It’s for charity and good fellowship. The rules say so.

events.label: Shafter says the order is a murder society in this place

communicates.speaker: jake_shafter
communicates.content: It’s a murder society, that’s vat it is.

events.label: McMurdo challenges Shafter to prove the claim and demands an apology or explanation

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: See here! I want you to take back what you’ve said, or else make it good. One or the other you must do before I quit this room. Put yourself in my place. Here am I, a stranger in the town. I belong to a society that I know only as an innocent one. You’ll find it through the length and breadth of the States, but always as an innocent one. Now, when I am counting upon joining it here, you tell me that it is the same as a murder society called the Scowrers. I guess you owe me either an apology or else an explanation, Mr. Shafter.

events.label: Shafter states that the bosses of the order and the Scowrers are the same and that offenders are struck by the other group

communicates.speaker: jake_shafter
communicates.content: I can but tell you vat the whole vorld knows, mister. The bosses of the one are the bosses of the other. If you offend the one, it is the other vat vill strike you. We have proved it too often.

events.label: McMurdo demands proof of the gossip.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: That’s just gossip—I want proof!

events.label: Mr. Shafter tells McMurdo he must leave and cannot stay there.

communicates.speaker: mr_shafter
communicates.content: If you live here long you vill get your proof. But I forget that you are yourself one of them. You vill soon be as bad as the rest. But you vill find other lodgings, mister. I cannot have you here. Is it not bad enough that one of these people come courting my Ettie, and that I dare not turn him down, but that I should have another for my boarder? Yes, indeed, you shall not sleep here after to-night!

events.label: McMurdo is placed under banishment from his room and from Ettie.
McMurdo speaks privately with Ettie in the sitting-room.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Sure, your father is after giving me notice. It’s little I would care if it was just my room, but indeed, Ettie, though it’s only a week that I’ve known you, you are the very breath of life to me, and I can’t live without you!

events.label: Ettie tells McMurdo that he is too late and that another man exists.

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Oh, hush, Mr. McMurdo, don’t speak so! I have told you, have I not, that you are too late? There is another, and if I have not promised to marry him at once, at least I can promise no one else.

events.label: McMurdo proposes that Ettie choose him instead of keeping the promise.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Suppose I had been first, Ettie, would I have had a chance?

events.label: McMurdo kneels before Ettie and asks her to choose him and leave with him.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: For God’s sake, Ettie, let it stand at that! Will you ruin your life and my own for the sake of this promise? Follow your heart, acushla! ’Tis a safer guide than any promise before you knew what it was that you were saying. Say that you will be mine, and we will face it out together!

events.label: Ettie refuses to say yes while they are there.

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Not here? No, no, Jack!

events.label: McMurdo holds Ettie in his arms and insists that it must be here.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Yes, here. It could not be here. Could you take me away? No, here. I’ll hold you against the world, Ettie, right here where we are!

events.label: Ettie asks why they should not leave together and McMurdo refuses to leave.

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Why should we not leave together?

events.label: Ettie names Baldwin, McGinty, and the Scowrers as people McMurdo does not know.

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: You don’t know, Jack. You’ve been here too short a time. You don’t know this Baldwin. You don’t know McGinty and his Scowrers.

events.label: McMurdo rejects fear of Baldwin, McGinty, and the Scowrers.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: No, I don’t know them, and I don’t fear them, and I don’t believe in them! I’ve lived among rough men, my darling, and instead of fearing them it has always ended that they have feared me—always, Ettie. It’s mad on the face of it! If these men, as your father says, have done crime after crime in the valley, and if everyone knows them by name, how comes it that none are brought to justice? You answer me that, Ettie!

events.label: Ettie explains that no witness dares testify and that the accused are protected by alibis.

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Because no witness dares to appear against them. He would not live a month if he did. Also because they have always their own men to swear that the accused one was far from the scene of the crime. But surely, Jack, you must have read all this. I had understood that every paper in the United States was writing about it.

events.label: Ettie tells Jack that she loathes Baldwin, fears him, and has been using half-promises to put him off.

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: now I can tell you the truth. I loathe him with all my heart; but I fear him also. I fear him for myself; but above all I fear him for father. I know that some great sorrow would come upon us if I dared to say what I really felt. That is why I have put him off with half-promises. It was in real truth our only hope.

events.label: Ettie asks Jack to flee with her and take her father away from the power of the wicked men.

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: if you would fly with me, Jack, we could take father with us and live forever far from the power of these wicked men.

events.label: Baldwin enters the room swaggering and confronts McMurdo and Ettie.
Ettie greets Baldwin, says he has arrived earlier than expected, and invites him to sit down.

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: I'm glad to see you, Mr. Baldwin. You're earlier than I had thought. Come and sit down.

events.label: Baldwin asks who McMurdo is.

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: Who is this?

events.label: Ettie introduces McMurdo to Baldwin as a friend and a new boarder.

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: It's a friend of mine, Mr. Baldwin, a new boarder here. Mr. McMurdo, may I introduce you to Mr. Baldwin?

events.label: McMurdo and Baldwin nod surlily to each other.
Baldwin asserts that Ettie belongs to him and orders McMurdo to take a walk.

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: Maybe Miss Ettie has told you how it is with us? I didn't understand that there was any relation between you. Didn't you? Well, you can understand it now. You can take it from me that this young lady is mine, and you'll find it a very fine evening for a walk.

events.label: McMurdo refuses Baldwin's suggestion of a walk.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Thank you, I am in no humour for a walk.

events.label: Baldwin challenges McMurdo to a fight.

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: Maybe you are in a humour for a fight, Mr. Boarder!

events.label: McMurdo accepts Baldwin's challenge.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: That I am! You never said a more welcome word.

events.label: Ettie begs Jack and Ted to stop fighting and urges Ted to be forgiving.

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: For God's sake, Jack! Oh, for God's sake! Oh, Jack, Jack, he will hurt you! Oh, it's Jack, is it? You've come to that already, have you? Oh, Ted, be reasonable—be kind! For my sake, Ted, if ever you loved me, be big-hearted and forgiving!

events.label: McMurdo tells Ettie to leave so that he and Baldwin can settle the matter.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I think, Ettie, that if you were to leave us alone we could get this thing settled. Or maybe, Mr. Baldwin, you will take a turn down the street with me. It's a fine evening, and there's some open ground beyond the next block.

events.label: His enemy threatens revenge without using his hands

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: I’ll get even with you without needing to dirty my hands. You’ll wish you had never set foot in this house before I am through with you!

events.label: McMurdo challenges the enemy to act at once

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: No time like the present.

events.label: The enemy responds and shows a branded sign on his forearm

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: I’ll choose my own time, mister. You can leave the time to me. See here! D’you know what that means? Well, you will know, I’ll promise you that. You won’t be much older, either. Perhaps Miss Ettie can tell you something about it. —on your knees—and then I’ll tell you what your punishment may be. You’ve sowed—and by the Lord, I’ll see that you reap!

events.label: The enemy leaves the house in fury
McMurdo and the girl stand in silence
The girl embraces McMurdo and urges him to flee that night

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Oh, Jack, how brave you were! But it is no use, you must fly! To-night—Jack—to-night! It’s your only hope. He will have your life. I read it in his horrible eyes. What chance have you against a dozen of them, with Boss McGinty and all the power of the lodge behind them?

events.label: McMurdo disengages her hands, kisses her, and sets her back into a chair
McMurdo says he is a Freeman and plans to sleep there that night

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: There, acushla, there! Don’t be disturbed or fear for me. I’m a Freeman myself. I’m after telling your father about it. Maybe I am no better than the others; so don’t make a saint of me. Perhaps you hate me too, now that I’ve told you as much? I was thinking the same thing. I’ll go right now and fix it. You can tell your father that I’ll sleep here to-night and find some other quarters in the morning.

events.label: The girl reassures McMurdo and urges him to seek McGinty first

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Hate you, Jack? While life lasts I could never do that! I’ve heard that there is no harm in being a Freeman anywhere but here; so why should I think the worse of you for that? But if you are a Freeman, Jack, why should you not go down and make a friend of Boss McGinty? Oh, hurry, Jack, hurry! Get your word in first, or the hounds will be on your trail.

events.label: McMurdo goes to McGinty’s saloon
McGinty is described as a popular but feared official whose bar is crowded
Boss McGinty's saloon grows larger and more ornate over time
McMurdo enters the saloon and moves through the crowd
McMurdo approaches McGinty at the far end of the saloon
McMurdo pushes through the courtiers toward McGinty
McMurdo and McGinty exchange greetings and remarks

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Well, young man, I can’t call your face to mind.

events.label: A voice identifies McGinty as Councillor McGinty

communicates.speaker: courtiers
communicates.content: He’s Councillor McGinty, young man.

events.label: McMurdo states that he is new there and was advised to see McGinty

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’m new here, Mr. McGinty. I’m sorry, Councillor. I’m strange to the ways of the place. But I was advised to see you.

events.label: McGinty asks who advised McMurdo to see him

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: And who told you?

events.label: McMurdo identifies Brother Scanlan of Lodge 341, Vermissa as the adviser and drinks McGinty's health

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Brother Scanlan of Lodge 341, Vermissa. I drink your health Councillor, and to our better acquaintance.

events.label: McGinty reacts to McMurdo's manner

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Oh, it’s like that, is it? I’ll have to look a bit closer into this, Mister—

events.label: McGinty calls McMurdo into the room behind the bar
McGinty closes the door and sits on a barrel while inspecting McMurdo in silence
McGinty produces a revolver and threatens McMurdo

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: See here, my joker, if I thought you were playing any game on us, it would be short work for you.

events.label: McMurdo says he is a stranger brother and McGinty demands proof of lodge membership

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: This is a strange welcome, for the Bodymaster of a lodge of Freemen to give to a stranger brother.

events.label: McMurdo answers McGinty's lodge questions about his initiation details

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Lodge 29, Chicago. June 24, 1872. James H. Scott. Bartholomew Wilson.

events.label: McGinty questions McMurdo about his work, his lodge, and why he left Chicago

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: What are you doing here? What are you doing here? Have you heard anything of the lodge in these parts? Why did you leave Chicago?

events.label: McMurdo shows McGinty a newspaper cutting about Jonas Pinto

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: You wouldn't squeal on a fellow? Look at that clipping.

events.label: McGinty reacts angrily to McMurdo's wording and then examines the clipping

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: You are right, Councillor.

events.label: McMurdo explains that he shot Jonas Pinto and fled to the coal country

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I was helping Uncle Sam to make dollars. This man Pinto helped me to shove the queer. Then he said he would split. Maybe he did split. I didn't wait to see. I just killed him and lighted out for the coal country. 'Cause I'd read in the papers that they weren't too particular in those parts. That's about the size of it.

events.label: McMurdo takes half a dozen coins from his pocket
McGinty holds the coins to the light in his hand
McGinty praises McMurdo as a useful brother and says the lodge can use bad men

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: you’ll be a mighty useful brother; we can do with a bad man or two among us, Friend McMurdo; for there are times when we have to take our own part; we’d soon be against the wall if we didn’t shove back at those that were pushing us

events.label: McMurdo agrees to do his share of shoving

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: I’ll do my share of shoving with the rest of the boys

events.label: McGinty says McMurdo has good nerve and mentions the gun he shoved at him

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: You seem to have a good nerve. You didn’t squirm when I shoved this gun at you.

events.label: McMurdo says he was covering McGinty with a cocked pistol

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: It was not me that was in danger. It was you, Councillor. I was covering you all the time. I guess my shot would have been as quick as yours.

events.label: McGinty laughs after flushing angry red
The bartender reports that Ted Baldwin must see McGinty at once

communicates.speaker: bartender
communicates.content: it’s Ted Baldwin. He says he must see you this very minute

events.label: Ted Baldwin enters, pushes the bartender out, and closes the door
Ted Baldwin says he has a word to say to McGinty about McMurdo

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: you got here first, did you? I’ve a word to say to you, Councillor, about this man

events.label: McMurdo challenges Baldwin to say it in front of him

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: Then say it here and now before my face

events.label: McGinty tries to reconcile McMurdo and Baldwin

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: This will never do. We have a new brother here, Baldwin, and it’s not for us to greet him in such fashion. Hold out your hand, man, and make it up

events.label: McMurdo says he will fight Baldwin in any manner Baldwin chooses

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: I’ve offered to fight him if he thinks I have wronged him. I’ll fight him with fists, or, if that won’t satisfy him, I’ll fight him any other way he chooses. Now, I’ll leave it to you, Councillor, to judge between us as a Bodymaster should

events.label: McMurdo says the dispute concerns a young lady who is free to choose for herself

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: A young lady. She’s free to choose for herself

events.label: McGinty rules that the young lady is free as between two lodge brothers

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: As between two brothers of the lodge I should say that she was. Yes, it is, Ted Baldwin. Is it you that would dispute it?

events.label: Baldwin accuses McGinty of choosing McMurdo over him

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: You would throw over one that has stood by you this five years in favour of a man that you never saw before in your life? You’re not Bodymaster for life, Jack McGinty, and by God! when next it comes to a vote—

events.label: McGinty attacks Baldwin and hurls him across a barrel
McMurdo pulls McGinty back to stop him from killing Baldwin
McGinty releases Baldwin and Baldwin sits up on the barrel, shaken and gasping
McGinty confronts Baldwin and then briefly reconciles with him over lodge discipline

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: You’ve been asking for it this many a day, Ted Baldwin—now you’ve got it! Maybe you think if I was voted down from Bodymaster you would find yourself in my shoes. It’s for the lodge to say that. But so long as I am the chief I’ll have no man lift his voice against me or my rulings. Well, then, we are all good friends again and there’s an end of the matter. That’s the end of the black blood. You come under lodge discipline if it goes further, and that’s a heavy hand in these parts, as Brother Baldwin knows—and as you will damn soon find out, Brother McMurdo, if you ask for trouble!

events.label: Baldwin answers McGinty

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: I have nothing against you. The clouds are heavy. But they will forever brighten. And this I swear!

events.label: McGinty pours champagne and the men drink a reconciliation toast

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: See now. Let us drink the quarrelling toast of the lodge. After that, as you know, there can be no bad blood between us. Now, then the left hand on the apple of my throat. I say to you, Ted Baldwin, what is the offense, sir?

events.label: McMurdo responds and takes Baldwin's hand

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Faith, I’d be slow to do that. I’m quick to quarrel and quick to forgive. It’s my hot Irish blood, they tell me. But it’s over for me, and I bear no grudge.

events.label: McGinty explains the women are outside lodge jurisdiction and tells McMurdo to join Lodge 341

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Tut! These girls! These girls! To think that the same petticoats should come between two of my boys! It’s the devil’s own luck! Well, it’s the colleen inside of them that must settle the question; for it’s outside the jurisdiction of a Bodymaster—and the Lord be praised for that! We have enough on us, without the women as well. You’ll have to be affiliated to Lodge 341, Brother McMurdo. We have our own ways and methods, different from Chicago. Saturday night is our meeting, and if you come then, we’ll make you free forever of the Vermissa Valley.

events.label: McMurdo moves his lodgings to Widow MacNamara's and later lodges with Scanlan
McMurdo continues to dine at Shafter's and see Ettie
McMurdo shows the coining moulds to lodge brothers and they take examples of false money
A mine police captain enters McGinty's saloon and orders whisky

communicates.speaker: teddy_marvin
communicates.content: A straight whisky; for the night is bitter.

events.label: McGinty speaks coldly to Captain Marvin about township police and capitalists

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: We’d do better without you, Captain Marvin, for we have our own police of the township, and no need for any imported goods. What are you but the paid tool of the capitalists, hired by them to club or shoot your poorer fellow citizen?

events.label: Marvin replies that they will not argue about the matter

communicates.speaker: teddy_marvin
communicates.content: Well, well, we won’t argue about that. I expect we all do our duty same as we see it; but we can’t all see it the same.

events.label: Marvin recognizes Jack McMurdo and addresses him as an old acquaintance

communicates.speaker: teddy_marvin
communicates.content: Hullo! Hullo! Here’s an old acquaintance!

events.label: McMurdo rejects friendship with Marvin and denies shame over his name

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I was never a friend to you nor any other cursed copper in my life. I'm not denying it. D’ye think I’m ashamed of my own name? What the devil d’you mean by that?

events.label: Marvin says he had been a Chicago officer and calls McMurdo a Chicago crook

communicates.speaker: teddy_marvin
communicates.content: No, no, Jack, bluster won’t do with me. I was an officer in Chicago before ever I came to this darned coal bunker, and I know a Chicago crook when I see one. Just the same old Teddy Marvin, at your service. We haven’t forgotten the shooting of Jonas Pinto up there. Did you not? That’s good impartial evidence, ain’t it? Well, his death came in uncommon handy for you, or they would have had you for shoving the queer. Well, we can let that be bygones; for, between you and me—and perhaps I’m going further than my duty in saying it—they could get no clear case against you, and Chicago’s open to you to-morrow.

events.label: McMurdo is spoken to by the captain and replies politely enough

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, I suppose you mean well, and I do thank you.

events.label: The captain warns McMurdo about living on the straight and leaves the bar-room
McMurdo becomes a local hero in the bar-room
The bar loafers crowd round McMurdo and shake his hand
McMurdo is introduced to the lodge
The lodge assembly meets at the Union House
Members assemble in the lodge room around the long table
McMurdo is led into an outer room by two solemn brothers
McMurdo hears voices from the assembly inside the partition
An inner guard enters and delivers the Bodymaster's order to truss, blind, and enter McMurdo

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: that he shall be trussed, blinded, and entered

events.label: Three men remove McMurdo's coat, turn up his sleeve, and bind his arms with a rope
A thick black cap is placed over McMurdo's head and face
McMurdo is led into the assembly hall
McGinty asks McMurdo whether he is already a member of the Ancient Order of Freemen

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: John McMurdo, are you already a member of the Ancient Order of Freemen?

events.label: McGinty asks McMurdo whether his lodge is No. 29, Chicago

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Is your lodge No. 29, Chicago?

events.label: McGinty and McMurdo exchange remarks about dark nights and heavy clouds

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Dark nights are unpleasant.

events.label: McGinty asks whether the brethren are satisfied

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: Are the brethren satisfied?

events.label: McGinty states that they know McMurdo is one of them by his sign and countersign and asks if he is ready to be tested

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: We know, Brother, by your sign and by your countersign that you are indeed one of us. We would have you know, however, that in this county and in other counties of these parts we have certain rites, and also certain duties of our own which call for good men. Are you ready to be tested?

events.label: McMurdo steps forward to prove his stout heart
McMurdo is subjected to a pain test on his forearm
The lodge audience applauds McMurdo's first appearance
McGinty questions McMurdo about the oath and the Bodymaster's rule

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: You have already sworn the oath of secrecy and fidelity, and you are aware that the punishment for any breach of it is instant and inevitable death? And you accept the rule of the Bodymaster for the time being under all circumstances?

events.label: McGinty welcomes McMurdo to Lodge 341 and orders liquor to be brought

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: In the name of Lodge 341, Vermissa, I welcome you to its privileges and debates. You will put the liquor on the table, Brother Scanlan, and we will drink to our worthy brother.

events.label: McMurdo examines his branded forearm after receiving his coat
The lodge proceeds with business after the initiation drinks are finished
McGinty reads Windle's letter about a job on Andrew Rae

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: There is a job to be done on Andrew Rae of Rae & Sturmash, coal owners near this place. You will remember that your lodge owes us a return, having had the service of two brethren in the matter of the patrolman last fall. You will send two good men, they will be taken charge of by Treasurer Higgins of this lodge, whose address you know. He will show them when to act and where.

events.label: McGinty asks for volunteers and several young fellows offer themselves
McGinty selects Tiger Cormac and Wilson for the job and discusses their participation

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: You’ll do, Tiger Cormac. If you handle it as well as you did the last, you won’t be wrong. And you, Wilson. It’s your first, is it not? Well, you have to be blooded some time. It will be a great start for you. As to the pistol, you’ll find it waiting for you, or I’m mistaken. If you report yourselves on Monday, it will be time enough. You’ll get a great welcome when you return.

events.label: Cormac asks about a reward for the job

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Any reward this time?

events.label: McGinty replies that the job is for honour and may yield a few dollars

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: Never mind the reward. You just do it for the honour of the thing. Maybe when it is done there will be a few odd dollars at the bottom of the box.

events.label: Wilson asks what the man has done and McGinty refuses to explain

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: Sure, it’s not for the likes of you to ask what the man has done. He has been judged over there. That’s no business of ours. All we have to do is to carry it out for them, same as they would for us.

events.label: McGinty says two brothers from the Merton lodge will come next week to do business

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: Two brothers from the Merton lodge are coming over to us next week to do some business in this quarter.

events.label: Someone asks who they are.

communicates.speaker: unknown
communicates.content: Who are they?

events.label: A speaker warns that it is wiser not to ask and says the men will make a clean job when they are about it.

communicates.speaker: unknown
communicates.content: Faith, it is wiser not to ask. If you know nothing, you can testify nothing, and no trouble can come of it. But they are men who will make a clean job when they are about it.

events.label: Ted Baldwin speaks about people getting out of hand and mentions three men being turned off by Foreman Blaker.

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: Folk are gettin’ out of hand in these parts. It was only last week that three of our men were turned off by Foreman Blaker. It’s been owing him a long time, and he’ll get it full and proper.

events.label: McMurdo whispers to his neighbour and asks what is meant by the reference to 'the business end of a buckshot cartridge'.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Get what?

events.label: A man answers with a loud laugh.
McMurdo says he likes the lodge ways and that it is a proper place for a lad of mettle.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I like it well. ’Tis a proper place for a lad of mettle.

events.label: Those around him applaud McMurdo's words.
The black-maned Bodymaster from the end of the table reacts to McMurdo's words.
McMurdo rises and offers to help the lodge if a man should be wanted.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I would say, Eminent Bodymaster, that if a man should be wanted I should take it as an honour to be chosen to help the lodge.

events.label: The meeting applauds McMurdo's offer.
The secretary moves that Brother McMurdo should wait until the lodge chooses to employ him.

communicates.speaker: harraway
communicates.content: that Brother McMurdo should wait until it is the good pleasure of the lodge to employ him.

events.label: McMurdo accepts waiting for the lodge's decision.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Sure, that was what I meant; I’m in your hands.

events.label: The chairman tells McMurdo his time will come and that he may come to a small matter that night.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: Your time will come, Brother. We have marked you down as a willing man, and we believe that you will do good work in these parts. There is a small matter to-night in which you may take a hand if it so please you. You can come to-night, anyhow, and it will help you to know what we stand for in this community. I will make the announcement later.

events.label: The chairman announces that he will ask the treasurer about the bank balance and mentions the pension to Jim Carnaway's widow.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: First of all, I will ask the treasurer as to our bank balance. There is the pension to Jim Carnaway’s widow. He was struck down doing the work of the lodge, and it is for us to see that she is not the loser.

events.label: McMurdo's neighbour explains that Jim was shot when men tried to kill Chester Wilcox of Marley Creek.

communicates.speaker: james_h_scott
communicates.content: Jim was shot last month when they tried to kill Chester Wilcox of Marley Creek.

events.label: The treasurer reports the funds are good and lists payments and threats against firms.

communicates.speaker: treasurer_higgins
communicates.content: The funds are good at the moment. The firms have been generous of late. Max Linder & Co. paid five hundred to be left alone. Walker Brothers sent in a hundred; but I took it on myself to return it and ask for five. If I do not hear by Wednesday, their winding gear may get out of order. We had to burn their breaker last year before they became reasonable. Then the West Section Coaling Company has paid its annual contribution. We have enough on hand to meet any obligations.

events.label: A brother asks about Archie Swindon.
The treasurer says Archie Swindon sold out and left the district and left a note.

communicates.speaker: treasurer_higgins
communicates.content: He has sold out and left the district. The old devil left a note for us to say that he had rather be a free crossing sweeper in New York than a large mine owner under the power of a ring of blackmailers. By Gar! it was as well that he made a break for it before the note reached us! I guess he won’t show his face in this valley again.

events.label: Brother Morris rises from the table end and asks who bought the property of the man driven out of the district

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: may I ask who has bought the property of this man that we have driven out of the district?

events.label: The treasurer answers that the State & Merton County Railroad Company bought the property

communicates.speaker: treasurer
communicates.content: It has been bought by the State & Merton County Railroad Company.

events.label: Brother Morris asks who bought the mines of Todman and Lee

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: And who bought the mines of Todman and of Lee that came into the market in the same way last year?

events.label: The treasurer answers that the same company bought the mines of Todman and Lee

communicates.speaker: treasurer
communicates.content: The same company, Brother Morris.

events.label: Brother Morris asks who bought several ironworks that were given up of late

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: And who bought the ironworks of Manson and of Shuman and of Van Deher and of Atwood, which have all been given up of late?

events.label: The treasurer answers that the West Gilmerton General Mining Company bought the ironworks

communicates.speaker: treasurer
communicates.content: They were all bought by the West Gilmerton General Mining Company.

events.label: Brother Morris argues that the lodge has driven small men out of trade and is making itself dangerous

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: With all respect to you, Eminent Bodymaster, I think it may matter very much to us. This process has been going on now for ten long years. We are gradually driving all the small men out of trade. What is the result? We find in their places great companies like the Railroad or the General Iron, who have their directors in New York or Philadelphia, and care nothing for our threats. We can take it out of their local bosses; but it only means that others will be sent in their stead. And we are making it dangerous for ourselves. The small men could not harm us. They had not the money nor the power. So long as we did not squeeze them too dry, they would stay on under our power. But if these big companies find that we stand between them and their profits, they will spare no pains and no expense to hunt us down and bring us to court.

events.label: The speaker resumes his seat and the lodge reacts with angry cries
McGinty rises and speaks to the lodge about unity and business for the evening

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Brother Morris, you were always a croaker. So long as the members of this lodge stand together there is no power in the United States that can touch them. Sure, have we not tried it often enough in the lawcourts? I expect the big companies will find it easier to pay than to fight, same as the little companies do. And now, Brethren, this lodge has finished its business for the evening, save for one small matter which may be mentioned when we are parting. The time has now come for fraternal refreshment and for harmony.

events.label: McMurdo sings for the lodge and wins its good will
The new recruit becomes popular among the brethren and is marked for advancement
McGinty addresses the men about James Stanger and his article

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: there is one man in this town that wants trimming up; James Stanger of the Herald has been opening his mouth against us again; the paper heads an article 'Law and Order!' and quotes 'Reign of Terror in the Coal and Iron District' describing our organization as responsible for assassinations, outrages, tyranny, terrorism, and lawlessness; the men are known; the organization is patent and public; the question is what shall we say to him?

events.label: The men murmur assent and mutter oaths
McGinty reads from the newspaper cutting and dismisses it

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Law and Order! Reign of Terror in the Coal and Iron District. Twelve years have now elapsed since the first assassinations which proved the existence of a criminal organization in our midst. From that day these outrages have never ceased, until now they have reached a pitch which makes us the opprobrium of the civilized world. Is it for such results as this that our great country welcomes to its bosom the alien who flies from the despotisms of Europe? Is it that they shall themselves become tyrants over the very men who have given them shelter, and that a state of terrorism and lawlessness should be established under the very shadow of the sacred folds of the starry Flag of Freedom which would raise horror in our minds if we read of it as existing under the most effete monarchy of the East? The men are known. The organization is patent and public. How long are we to endure it? Can we forever live—

events.label: A dozen men cry out to kill James Stanger

communicates.speaker: freeman_organisation
communicates.content: Kill him!

events.label: Brother Morris protests against killing James Stanger

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: our hand is too heavy in this valley, and there will come a point where in self-defense every man will unite to crush us out. James Stanger is an old man. He is respected in the township and the district. His paper stands for all that is solid in the valley. If that man is struck down, there will be a stir through this state that will only end with our destruction.

events.label: McGinty challenges Morris on how destruction would come about

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Is it by the police? Sure, half of them are in our pay and half of them afraid of us. Or is it by the law courts and the judge? Haven't we tried that before now, and what ever came of it?

events.label: Brother Morris mentions Judge Lynch

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: There is a Judge Lynch that might try the case.

events.label: McGinty threatens Morris and says he has him under watch

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: I have but to raise my finger, and I could put two hundred men into this town that would clear it out from end to end. See here, Brother Morris, I have my eye on you, and have had for some time! You’ve no heart yourself, and you try to take the heart out of others. It will be an ill day for you, Brother Morris, when your own name comes on our agenda paper, and I’m thinking that it’s just there that I ought to place it.

events.label: Morris recoils and sits back in his chair
Morris drinks from his glass before answering
Morris apologizes to the Eminent Bodymaster and the lodge brethren and promises not to offend again

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: I apologize, Eminent Bodymaster, to you and to every brother in this lodge if I have said more than I should. I am a faithful member—you all know that—and it is my fear lest evil come to the lodge which makes me speak in anxious words. But I have greater trust in your judgment than in my own, Eminent Bodymaster, and I promise you that I will not offend again.

events.label: The Bodymaster relaxes his scowl while listening
The Bodymaster responds that the lodge will remain united and that Stanger should receive a severe warning

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: Very good, Brother Morris. It’s myself that would be sorry if it were needful to give you a lesson. But so long as I am in this chair we shall be a united lodge in word and in deed. And now, boys, I’ll say this much, that if Stanger got his full deserts there would be more trouble than we need ask for. These editors hang together, and every journal in the state would be crying out for police and troops. But I guess you can give him a pretty severe warning. Will you fix it, Brother Baldwin?

events.label: Ted Baldwin agrees to fix the matter

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: Sure!

events.label: The chairman says the new brother may come

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: I promised the new brother he should go.

events.label: The chairman orders the group to get to work

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: That’s enough. The sooner we get to work the better.

events.label: The company breaks up in shouts, yells, and drunken song
The duty band leaves the bar and goes out into the street
The men gather in a yard facing a high building and see the Vermissa Herald sign and hear printing from within
Baldwin assigns McMurdo to stand below at the door while he takes the others inside

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: You can stand below at the door and see that the road is kept open for us. Arthur Willaby can stay with you. You others come with me. Have no fears, boys; for we have a dozen witnesses that we are in the Union Bar at this very moment.

events.label: The party crosses the road and Baldwin's men rush into the newspaper office
McMurdo and another man remain below
A struggle erupts upstairs and a gray-haired man rushes onto the landing, is seized, struck down, and beaten
McMurdo rushes up the stair and pushes Baldwin back
Baldwin warns that the man will be killed and orders the weapon dropped.

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: You’ll kill the man. Drop it!

events.label: Baldwin looks at McMurdo in amazement.
Baldwin shouts abuse and orders McMurdo to stand back.

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: Curse you! Who are you to interfere—you that are new to the lodge? Stand back!

events.label: The man raises his stick and McMurdo draws his pistol.
McMurdo warns the man to stand back and threatens to shoot him.

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: Stand back yourself! I’ll blow your face in if you lay a hand on me. As to the lodge, wasn’t it the order of the Bodymaster that the man was not to be killed—and what are you doing but killing him?

events.label: One of the men remarks that McMurdo is speaking the truth.

communicates.speaker: one_of_the_men
communicates.content: It’s truth he says.

events.label: The man below urges the others to hurry because the windows are lighting up and the town will soon arrive.

communicates.speaker: the_dead_man
communicates.content: By Gar! you’d best hurry yourselves! The windows are all lighting up, and you’ll have the whole town here inside of five minutes.

events.label: Shouting breaks out in the street and a group of compositors and pressmen gathers in the hall below.
The criminals leave the editor's body and flee down the stairs into the street.
Some of the men mix with the crowd in McGinty's saloon and whisper to the Boss that the job was carried through.

communicates.speaker: some_of_the_men
communicates.content: the job had been well carried through

events.label: Others, including McMurdo, break away into side streets and go home by devious paths.
McMurdo wakes the next morning after his initiation into the lodge.
McMurdo has a headache and a hot, swollen branded arm.
McMurdo stays at home for the morning, writes a long letter, and later reads the Daily Herald.
McMurdo reads the Herald report about the office outrage and Stanger's injuries.
McMurdo lays down the paper and lights his pipe when his landlady brings him an unsigned note.
McMurdo reads the note directing him to Miller Hill by the flagstaff.
McMurdo strolls up the path to the restaurant on Miller Hill
McMurdo meets Brother Morris at Miller Hill and they exchange the lodge sign
Brother Morris speaks privately with McMurdo

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: I wanted to have a word with you, Mr. McMurdo. It was kind of you to come. Why did you not put your name to the note? One has to be cautious, mister. One never knows in times like these how a thing may come back to one. One never knows either who to trust or who not to trust. No, no, not always. Whatever we say, even what we think, seems to go back to that man McGinty. Look here! It was only last night, as you know well, that I swore good faith to our Bodymaster. Would you be asking me to break my oath? If that is the view you take, I can only say that I am sorry I gave you the trouble to come and meet me. Things have come to a bad pass when two free citizens cannot speak their thoughts to each other. And to take it back to Boss McGinty! Indeed, then, you do me injustice there. For myself I am loyal to the lodge, and so I tell you straight; but I would be a poor creature if I were to repeat to any other what you might say to me in confidence. It will go no further than me; though I warn you that you may get neither help nor sympathy. I have given up looking for either the one or the other. I may be putting my very life in your hands by what I say; but, bad as you are—and it seemed to me last night that you were shaping to be as bad as the worst—still you are new to it, and your conscience cannot yet be as hardened as theirs. That was why I thought to speak with you. Well, what have you to say? If you give me away, may a curse be on you! Sure, I said I would not. I would ask you, then, when you joined the Freeman’s society in Chicago and swore vows of charity and fidelity, did ever it cross your mind that you might find it would lead you to crime?

events.label: McMurdo responds that if it is called crime, then it is called crime.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: If you call it crime.

events.label: Morris insists that the violence should be called crime.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: Call it crime! You have seen little of it if you can call it anything else. Was it crime last night when a man old enough to be your father was beaten till the blood dripped from his white hairs? Was that crime—or what else would you call it?

events.label: McMurdo describes the violence as a war between two classes.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: There are some would say it was war, a war of two classes with all in, so that each struck as best it could.

events.label: Morris asks whether McMurdo expected violence when he joined the Freeman’s society at Chicago.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: Well, did you think of such a thing when you joined the Freeman’s society at Chicago?

events.label: McMurdo denies that he thought of such violence when he joined.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: No, I’m bound to say I did not.

events.label: Morris says he joined the society in Philadelphia as a benefit club and meeting place.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: Nor did I when I joined it at Philadelphia. It was just a benefit club and a meeting place for one’s fellows.

events.label: Morris says he came to better himself, brought his family, started a drygoods store, and prospered.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: and I came to better myself! My wife and three children came with me. I started a drygoods store on Market Square, and I prospered well.

events.label: Morris says the word spread that he was a Freeman and he was forced to join the local lodge.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: The word had gone round that I was a Freeman, and I was forced to join the local lodge, same as you did last night.

events.label: Morris says he bears the lodge badge and an inner mark of shame.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: I’ve the badge of shame on my forearm and something worse branded on my heart.

events.label: Morris says he was under the orders of a black villain and caught in a meshwork of crime.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: I found that I was under the orders of a black villain and caught in a meshwork of crime.

events.label: Morris says every attempt to improve matters was treated as treason.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: What could I do? Every word I said to make things better was taken as treason, same as it was last night.

events.label: Morris says he cannot leave because his store contains all he owns and departure would mean murder to him and possibly to his family.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: I can’t get away; for all I have in the world is in my store. If I leave the society, I know well that it means murder to me, and God knows what to my wife and children. Oh, man, it is awful—awful!

events.label: Morris breaks down sobbing.
McMurdo tells Morris he was too soft for the job and the wrong sort for the work.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: You were too soft for the job. You are the wrong sort for such work.

events.label: Morris says his conscience and religion made him a criminal among them.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: I had a conscience and a religion; but they made me a criminal among them.

events.label: Morris says he was chosen for a job and went along despite fear of consequences.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: I was chosen for a job. If I backed down I knew well what would come to me. Maybe I’m a coward. Maybe it’s the thought of my poor little woman and the children that makes me one. Anyhow I went. I guess it will haunt me forever.

events.label: Morris describes a lonely house and says he was assigned to the door while others went in.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: It was a lonely house, twenty miles from here, over the range yonder. I was told off for the door, same as you were last night. They could not trust me with the job. The others went in.

events.label: Morris says the others came out with bloody hands and a child screamed from the house.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: When they came out their hands were crimson to the wrists. As we turned away a child was screaming out of the house behind us. It was a boy of five who had seen his father murdered.

events.label: Morris says he had to hide his horror to avoid retaliation against his family.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: I nearly fainted with the horror of it, and yet I had to keep a bold and smiling face; for well I knew that if I did not it would be out of my house that they would come next with their bloody hands and it would be my little Fred that would be screaming for his father.

events.label: Morris says he became a criminal, a sharer in murder, and was cut off from his faith.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: But I was a criminal then, part sharer in a murder, lost forever in this world, and lost also in the next. I am a good Catholic; but the priest would have no word with me when he heard I was a Scowrer, and I am excommunicated from my faith. That’s how it stands with me.

events.label: Morris warns McMurdo that he is going down the same road and asks how it will end.

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: I see you going down the same road, and I ask you what the end is to be. Are you ready to be a cold-blooded murderer also, or can we do anything to stop it?

events.label: McMurdo asks Morris what he would do and whether he would inform on someone; Morris rejects the idea of informing

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: What would you do? You would not inform?

events.label: McMurdo warns Morris that he is weak, says Morris should sell out sooner, and says Morris's statements are safe with him unless he is an informer

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’m thinking that you are a weak man and that you make too much of the matter. Too much! Wait till you have lived here longer. Look down the valley! See the cloud of a hundred chimneys that overshadows it! I tell you that the cloud of murder hangs thicker and lower than that over the heads of the people. It is the Valley of Fear, the Valley of Death. The terror is in the hearts of the people from the dusk to the dawn. Wait, young man, and you will learn for yourself. What is very clear is that you are not the man for the place, and that the sooner you sell out—if you only get a dime a dollar for what the business is worth—the better it will be for you. What you have said is safe with me; but, by Gar! if I thought you were an informer—

events.label: Morris pleads with McMurdo not to accuse him of being an informer

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: No, no!

events.label: McMurdo ends the talk, says he will remember it, says Morris meant kindly, and leaves for home

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, let it rest at that. I’ll bear what you have said in mind, and maybe some day I’ll come back to it. I expect you meant kindly by speaking to me like this. Now I’ll be getting home.

events.label: Morris warns McMurdo that they may have been seen together and that others may ask what they spoke about

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: One word before you go. We may have been seen together. They may want to know what we have spoken about.

events.label: Morris offers McMurdo a clerkship in his store and McMurdo refuses it

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: I offer you a clerkship in my store.

events.label: Boss McGinty visits McMurdo at his home and sits opposite him

communicates.speaker: boss_mcginty
communicates.content: I’m not much of a visitor, Brother McMurdo. I guess I am too busy over the folk that visit me. But I thought I’d stretch a point and drop down to see you in your own house.

events.label: McMurdo greets McGinty and brings out whisky
McGinty asks about McMurdo's arm and McMurdo says he is not forgetting it but it is worth it

communicates.speaker: boss_mcginty
communicates.content: How’s the arm?

events.label: McGinty says the arm is worth it for loyal men who help the lodge

communicates.speaker: boss_mcginty
communicates.content: Yes, it’s worth it, to those that are loyal and go through with it and are a help to the lodge.

events.label: McGinty asks what McMurdo was speaking to Brother Morris about on Miller Hill

communicates.speaker: boss_mcginty
communicates.content: What were you speaking to Brother Morris about on Miller Hill this morning?

events.label: McMurdo explains that Morris offered him a clerkship because Morris thought he was at a loose end, and that he refused it

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Morris didn’t know I could earn a living here at home. He shan’t know either; for he has got too much conscience for the likes of me. But he’s a good-hearted old chap. It was his idea that I was at a loose end, and that he would do me a good turn by offering me a clerkship in a drygoods store. Yes, that was it. Sure. Couldn’t I earn ten times as much in my own bedroom with four hours’ work?

events.label: McGinty agrees and tells McMurdo not to associate too much with Morris

communicates.speaker: boss_mcginty
communicates.content: That’s so. But I wouldn’t get about too much with Morris.

events.label: McMurdo and McGinty argue in the room.

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Why not? Well, I guess because I tell you not. That’s enough for most folk in these parts. Well, if you want reasons, I’ll give them. Did Morris say nothing to you against the lodge? No. Nor against me? No. Well, that’s because he daren’t trust you. But in his heart he is not a loyal brother. We know that well. So we watch him and we wait for the time to admonish him. I’m thinking that the time is drawing near. There’s no room for scabby sheep in our pen. But if you keep company with a disloyal man, we might think that you were disloyal, too. See? Well, that’s enough. I came down to give you a word in season, and you’ve had it. It’s my business to know what goes on in this township. I guess you’d best reckon on my hearing all that passes. Well, time’s up, and I’ll just say—

events.label: McMurdo says he dislikes Morris and denies disloyalty.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: There’s no chance of my keeping company with him; for I dislike the man. As to being disloyal, if it was any man but you he would not use the word to me twice. I’d like to know how you ever came to learn that I had spoken with Morris at all?

events.label: McGinty finishes his drink and is interrupted by police entering the room.
Captain Marvin and armed constables enter and confront McMurdo.

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: I thought you’d be getting into trouble, Mr. Crooked McMurdo of Chicago. Can’t keep out of it, can you? Take your hat and come along with us.

events.label: McGinty protests the police action and challenges Captain Marvin.

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: I guess you’ll pay for this, Captain Marvin. Who are you, I’d like to know, to break into a house in this fashion and molest honest, law-abiding men? He is a friend of mine, and I’ll answer for his conduct. By Gar! a man might as well live in Russia as in Vermissa while folk like you are running the police. It’s a capitalist outrage, and you’ll hear more of it, I reckon.

events.label: Captain Marvin states that the police are after McMurdo and orders him covered.

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: You’re standing out in this deal, Councillor McGinty. We are not out after you, but after this man McMurdo. It is for you to help, not to hinder us in our duty. By all accounts, Mr. McGinty, you may have to answer for your own conduct some of these days. This man McMurdo was a crook before ever he came here, and he’s a crook still. Cover him, Patrolman, while I disarm him.

events.label: McMurdo shows his pistol and taunts Captain Marvin.

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: There’s my pistol. Maybe, Captain Marvin, if you and I were alone and face to face you would not take me so easily. Where’s your warrant?

events.label: McMurdo asks what he is accused of

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: What am I accused of?

events.label: An accusation of involvement in the beating of Editor Stanger is stated
McGinty says McMurdo was with him in the saloon playing poker until midnight

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: This man was with me in my saloon playing poker up to midnight, and I can bring a dozen to prove it.

events.label: The captain orders McMurdo to come quietly under arrest

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Meanwhile, come on, McMurdo, and come quietly if you don’t want a gun across your head.

events.label: McMurdo and McGinty accept the situation
The boss whispers with McMurdo before they part

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: What about—

events.label: McMurdo indicates a safe hiding place under the floor

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: All right

events.label: The boss says good-bye and promises to see Reilly the lawyer

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: I’ll bid you good-bye. I’ll see Reilly the lawyer and take the defense upon myself. Take my word for it that they won’t be able to hold you.

Jack greets Ettie and reaches out to her

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: It’s you! And to think that you should come to me, heart of my heart, and I should find nothing better to do than to want to strangle you! Come then, darling, let me make it up to you.

events.label: Ettie questions Jack about his fear and the letter

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: What’s come over you, Jack? Why were you so scared of me? Oh, Jack, if your conscience was at ease, you would not have looked at me like that! Let me see that letter you were writing. It’s to another woman. I know it! Why else should you hold it from me? Was it to your wife that you were writing? How am I to know that you are not a married man—you, a stranger, that nobody knows?

events.label: Jack denies being married and explains that the letter is secret lodge business

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: I am not married, Ettie. See now, I swear it! You’re the only one woman on earth to me. By the cross of Christ I swear it! I’ll tell you, acushla. I’m under oath not to show it, and just as I wouldn’t break my word to you so I would keep it to those who hold my promise. It’s the business of the lodge, and even to you it’s secret. And if I was scared when a hand fell on me, can’t you understand it when it might have been the hand of a detective?

events.label: Jack embraces and kisses Ettie
Jack invites Ettie to sit beside him and speaks of her as his queen and lover

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Sit here by me, then. It’s a queer throne for such a queen; but it’s the best your poor lover can find. He’ll do better for you some of these days, I’m thinking. Now your mind is easy once again, is it not?

events.label: Ettie says Jack is a criminal among criminals and begs him to give it up

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: How can it ever be at ease, Jack, when I know that you are a criminal among criminals, when I never know the day that I may hear you are in court for murder? ‘McMurdo the Scowrer,’ that’s what one of our boarders called you yesterday. It went through my heart like a knife. But they were true. Give it up, Jack! For my sake, for God’s sake, give it up! It was to ask you that I came here to-day. Oh, Jack, see—I beg it of you on my bended knees! Kneeling here before you I implore you to give it up!

events.label: Jack refuses to abandon the oath and the lodge

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Sure, my darlin’, you don’t know what it is you are asking. How could I give it up when it would be to break my oath and to desert my comrades? If you could see how things stand with me you could never ask it of me. Besides, if I wanted to, how could I do it? You don’t suppose that the lodge would let a man go free with all its secrets?

events.label: Ettie says she has planned an escape with her father to a safer place

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: I’ve thought of that, Jack. I’ve planned it all. Father has saved some money. He is weary of this place where the fear of these people darkens our lives. He is ready to go. We would fly together to Philadelphia or New York, where we would be safe from them.

events.label: McMurdo laughs and warns that the lodge can reach distant places

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: The lodge has a long arm. Do you think it could not stretch from here to Philadelphia or New York?

events.label: Ettie proposes leaving for the West, England, Germany, or anywhere beyond the valley

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Well, then, to the West, or to England, or to Germany, where father came from—anywhere to get away from this Valley of Fear!

events.label: McMurdo thinks of old Brother Morris
McMurdo speaks about the valley being so named and the shadow on some people

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Sure, it is the second time I have heard the valley so named. The shadow does indeed seem to lie heavy on some of you.

events.label: Ettie says the valley darkens their lives and mentions Ted Baldwin

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: It darkens every moment of our lives. Do you suppose that Ted Baldwin has ever forgiven us? If it were not that he fears you, what do you suppose our chances would be? If you saw the look in those dark, hungry eyes of his when they fall on me!

events.label: McMurdo says he would punish Ted Baldwin if he caught him

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: By Gar! I’d teach him better manners if I caught him at it!

events.label: McMurdo refuses to leave immediately but offers to try to arrange an honorable departure

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: But see here, little girl. I can’t leave here. I can’t—take that from me once and for all. But if you will leave me to find my own way, I will try to prepare a way of getting honourably out of it. Well, well, it’s just how you look at it. But if you’ll give me six months, I’ll work it so that I can leave without being ashamed to look others in the face.

events.label: Ettie reacts with joy and asks whether McMurdo's offer is a promise

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Six months! Is it a promise?

events.label: McMurdo says the departure may take seven or eight months but will happen within a year

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, it may be seven or eight. But within a year at the furthest we will leave the valley behind us.

events.label: Scanlan speaks about past killings and keeping silent until the work is done

communicates.speaker: scanlan_lodge_341_vermissa
communicates.content: We are all in it together. That’s true enough, and we’ll talk till the cows come home of the killing of Charlie Williams or of Simon Bird, or any other job in the past. But till the work is done we say nothing.

events.label: McMurdo says he wants to speak to several people

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: There are half a dozen about here that I have a word to say to.

communicates.speaker: scanlan_lodge_341_vermissa
communicates.content: I suppose it isn’t Jack Knox of Ironhill that you are after. I’d go some way to see him get his deserts. Or Herman Strauss?

events.label: Boss McGinty says Chester Wilcox must be settled and can be found at the Iron Dike Company

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: We’ll never be right in this district until Chester Wilcox has been settled, and you’ll have the thanks of every lodge in the coal fields if you can down him. He’s the chief foreman of the Iron Dike Company. He’s a hard citizen, an old colour sergeant of the war, all scars and grizzle. We’ve had two tries at him; but had no luck, and Jim Carnaway lost his life over it. Now it’s for you to take it over. That’s the house—all alone at the Iron Dike crossroad, same as you see here on the map—without another within earshot. It’s no good by day. He’s armed and shoots quick and straight, with no questions asked. But at night—well, there he is with his wife, three children, and a hired help. You can’t pick or choose. It’s all or none. If you could get a bag of blasting powder at the front door with a slow match to it—

events.label: McGinty orders McMurdo to settle the matter by attacking Chester Wilcox's house

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: What’s the man done? Didn’t I tell you he shot Jim Carnaway? Why did he shoot him? Carnaway was about his house at night, and he shot him. That’s enough for me and you. You’ve got to settle the thing right. There’s these two women and the children. Do they go up too? They have to—else how can we get him? You’ll do it, then? Of course I will do it. When? Well, you had best give me a night or two that I may see the house and make my plans. Then— Very good. I leave it with you. It will be a great day when you bring us the news. It’s just the last stroke that will bring them all to their knees.
