events.label: Morris explains that the detective is not a man of the district and asks about Pinkerton's

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: No, no, it’s no man of the district. As you say, we know them, and it is little that they can do. But you’ve heard of Pinkerton’s?

events.label: McMurdo says he has read of some folk of that name

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’ve read of some folk of that name.

events.label: Morris warns that they have no chance if Pinkerton's are on their trail

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: Well, you can take it from me you’ve no show when they are on your trail. It’s not a take-it-or-miss-it government concern. It’s a dead earnest business proposition that’s out for results and keeps out till by hook or crook it gets them. If a Pinkerton man is deep in this business, we are all destroyed.

events.label: McMurdo says they must kill him

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: We must kill him.

events.label: Morris objects to identifying the man to be murdered and says it would end in murder

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: Ah, it’s the first thought that came to you! So it will be up at the lodge. Didn’t I say to you that it would end in murder? Sure, what is murder? Isn’t it common enough in these parts? It is, indeed; but it’s not for me to point out the man that is to be murdered. I’d never rest easy again. And yet it’s our own necks that may be at stake. In God’s name what shall I do?

events.label: Morris rocks to and fro in indecision
McMurdo is moved by Morris's words and grips his shoulder
McMurdo urges Morris to give the facts and asks who the fellow is, where he is, how he heard of him, and why he came

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: See here, man, you won’t gain anything by sitting keening like an old wife at a wake. Let’s have the facts. Who is the fellow? Where is he? How did you hear of him? Why did you come to me?

events.label: Morris explains why he came to McMurdo and gives the source of the letter

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_morris
communicates.content: I came to you; for you are the one man that would advise me. I told you that I had a store in the East before I came here. I left good friends behind me, and one of them is in the telegraph service. Here’s a letter that I had from him yesterday. It’s this part from the top of the page. You can read it yourself.

events.label: McMurdo reads the letter from Morris's friend
McMurdo sits in silence holding the letter and then asks whether anyone else knows of it

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Does anyone else know of this?

events.label: Morris asks whether the man has any other person he would likely write to

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: But this man—your friend—has he any other person that he would be likely to write to?

events.label: McMurdo says the man likely knows one or two more

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, I dare say he knows one or two more.

events.label: Morris asks whether the people are of the lodge

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: Of the lodge?

events.label: McMurdo says that is likely enough

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: It’s likely enough.

events.label: McMurdo explains that he asked because the man may have given a description of Birdy Edwards

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I was asking because it is likely that he may have given some description of this fellow Birdy Edwards—then we could get on his trail.

events.label: McMurdo says it is possible but he should not think the man knew Birdy Edwards

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, it’s possible. But I should not think he knew him.

events.label: McMurdo says the man is only telling him news that came by way of business

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: He is just telling me the news that came to him by way of business.

events.label: McMurdo asks how the man would know the Pinkerton man

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: How would he know this Pinkerton man?

events.label: McMurdo starts violently
McMurdo says he has got him and asks Morris to leave the matter in his hands

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: By Gar! I’ve got him. What a fool I was not to know it. Lord! but we’re in luck! We will fix him before he can do any harm. See here, Morris, will you leave this thing in my hands?

events.label: Morris agrees to leave the matter in McMurdo's hands

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: Sure, if you will only take it off mine. It’s just what I would ask.

events.label: McMurdo says he will take responsibility and tells Morris to keep silent

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I’ll do that. You can stand right back and let me run it. Even your name need not be mentioned. I’ll take it all on myself, as if it were to me that this letter has come. Will that content you? Then leave it at that and keep your head shut. Now I’ll get down to the lodge, and we’ll soon make old man Pinkerton sorry for himself.

events.label: Morris asks whether McMurdo would kill the man

communicates.speaker: morris
communicates.content: You wouldn’t kill this man?

events.label: McMurdo tells Morris not to ask questions and says he has hold of the matter

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: The less you know, Friend Morris, the easier your conscience will be, and the better you will sleep. Ask no questions, and let these things settle themselves. I have hold of it now.

events.label: Morris leaves sadly
McMurdo says self-protection is no murder and that it is him or us

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Self-protection is no murder, anyhow. It’s him or us. I guess this man would destroy us all if we left him long in the valley. Why, Brother Morris, we’ll have to elect you Bodymaster yet; for you’ve surely saved the lodge.

events.label: McMurdo destroys papers that would incriminate him
McMurdo stops at Shafter's house and Ettie comes out to him
Ettie says something has happened and that Jack is in danger

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Something has happened! Oh, Jack, you are in danger!

events.label: McMurdo says it may be wise to make a move before it is worse

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Sure, it is not very bad, my sweetheart. And yet it may be wise that we make a move before it is worse. Make a move?

events.label: McMurdo says he promised to go some day, had bad news, and sees trouble coming

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I promised you once that I would go some day. I think the time is coming. I had news to-night, bad news, and I see trouble coming. Well, a Pinkerton. But, sure, you wouldn’t know what that is, acushla, nor what it may mean to the likes of me. I’m too deep in this thing, and I may have to get out of it quick. You said you would come with me if I went.

events.label: Jack asks Ettie to trust him and promises not to harm her

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: I’m an honest man in some things, Ettie. I wouldn’t hurt a hair of your bonny head for all that the world can give, nor ever pull you down one inch from the golden throne above the clouds where I always see you. Would you trust me?

events.label: Ettie places her hand in Jack's hand
Jack orders Ettie to accompany him if he leaves

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: Well, then, listen to what I say, and do as I order you, for indeed it’s the only way for us. Things are going to happen in this valley. I feel it in my bones. There may be many of us that will have to look out for ourselves. I’m one, anyhow. If I go, by day or night, it’s you that must come with me!

events.label: Ettie says she would come after Jack

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: I’d come after you, Jack.

events.label: Jack insists Ettie must come with him and explains his plan to leave her until marriage

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: No, no, you shall come with me. If this valley is closed to me and I can never come back, how can I leave you behind, and me perhaps in hiding from the police with never a chance of a message? It’s with me you must come. I know a good woman in the place I come from, and it’s there I’d leave you till we can get married. Will you come?

events.label: Ettie agrees to come with Jack

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Yes, Jack, I will come.

events.label: Jack blesses Ettie and instructs her to go to the depot waiting room when signaled

communicates.speaker: jack
communicates.content: God bless you for your trust in me! It’s a fiend out of hell that I should be if I abused it. Now, mark you, Ettie, it will be just a word to you, and when it reaches you, you will drop everything and come right down to the waiting room at the depot and stay there till I come for you.

events.label: Ettie says she will come at the word

communicates.speaker: ettie_shafter
communicates.content: Day or night, I’ll come at the word, Jack.

events.label: McMurdo goes to the lodge
McMurdo passes through lodge guards using signs and countersigns
The lodge welcomes McMurdo
McMurdo sees lodge leaders assembled in the crowded room
The chairman speaks to McMurdo about business that needs judgment

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Indeed, it’s glad we are to see you, Brother! There’s business here that wants a Solomon in judgment to set it right.

events.label: A neighbour explains the dispute over the head money for Crabbe's shooting

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: It’s Lander and Egan. They both claim the head money given by the lodge for the shooting of old man Crabbe over at Stylestown, and who’s to say which fired the bullet?

events.label: McMurdo claims urgency before the lodge

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: Eminent Bodymaster, I claim urgency!

events.label: McMurdo presents ill news to the lodge about a planned destruction campaign and a Pinkerton detective in the valley

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: Eminent Bodymaster and Brethren, I am the bearer of ill news this day; but it is better that it should be known and discussed, than that a blow should fall upon us without warning which would destroy us all. I have information that the most powerful and richest organizations in this state have bound themselves together for our destruction, and that at this very moment there is a Pinkerton detective, one Birdy Edwards, at work in the valley collecting the evidence which may put a rope round the necks of many of us, and send every man in this room into a felon’s cell. That is the situation for the discussion of which I have made a claim of urgency.

events.label: The chairman breaks the dead silence in the room
The chairman asks McMurdo for his evidence

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: What is your evidence for this, Brother McMurdo?

events.label: McMurdo says the evidence is in a letter that has come into his hands

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: It is in this letter which has come into my hands.

events.label: McMurdo reads the passage from the letter aloud

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: It is a matter of honour with me that I can give no further particulars about the letter, nor put it into your hands; but I assure you that there is nothing else in it which can affect the interests of the lodge. I put the case before you as it has reached me.

events.label: An older brother says Birdy Edwards has the reputation of being the best man in the Pinkerton service

communicates.speaker: unknown
communicates.content: I have heard of Birdy Edwards, and that he has the name of being the best man in the Pinkerton service.

events.label: McGinty asks whether anyone knows Birdy Edwards by sight

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: Does anyone know him by sight?

events.label: McMurdo says that he knows Birdy Edwards by sight

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I do.

events.label: The hall reacts with astonishment
McMurdo says they can hold Birdy Edwards in their power and act quickly to end the matter

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I believe we hold him in the hollow of our hands. If we act quickly and wisely, we can cut this thing short. If I have your confidence and your help, it is little that we have to fear.

events.label: McGinty asks what they have to fear and what Birdy Edwards can know of their affairs

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: What have we to fear, anyhow? What can he know of our affairs?

events.label: McMurdo warns that Birdy Edwards has capitalist backing, may buy weaker brethren, and may already have their secrets

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: You might say so if all were as stanch as you, Councillor. But this man has all the millions of the capitalists at his back. Do you think there is no weaker brother among all our lodges that could not be bought? He will get at our secrets—maybe has got them already. There’s only one sure cure.

events.label: Baldwin says Birdy Edwards must never leave the valley

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin
communicates.content: That he never leaves the valley.

events.label: McMurdo approves Baldwin’s suggestion

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Good for you, Brother Baldwin. You and I have had our differences, but you have said the true word to-night.

events.label: McMurdo says the matter is too vital to discuss in open lodge and proposes a committee

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I would put it to you that this is too vital a thing for us to discuss in open lodge. God forbid that I should throw a doubt on anyone here; but if so much as a word of gossip got to the ears of this man, there would be an end of any chance of our getting him. I would ask the lodge to choose a trusty committee, Mr. Chairman—yourself, if I might suggest it, and Brother Baldwin here, and five more. Then I can talk freely of what I know and of what I advise should be done.

events.label: The lodge adopts the proposition and chooses a committee
The lodge’s revelry becomes short and subdued and the men break up early
McGinty and McMurdo speak alone after the others leave
McMurdo explains that Birdy Edwards is not present under that name and is lodging at Hobson’s Patch as Steve Wilson

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I said just now that I knew Birdy Edwards. I need not tell you that he is not here under that name. He’s a brave man, but not a crazy one. He passes under the name of Steve Wilson, and he is lodging at Hobson’s Patch.

events.label: A man tells how he met another man on the cars and took him for a reporter

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Because I fell into talk with him. I met him on the cars when I went down the line on Wednesday. He said he was a reporter. Wanted to know all he could about the Scowrers and what he called the outrages for a New York paper. He paid me twenty dollars for information and offered ten times that if I could find more.

events.label: A man says he gave the other man false information

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Any stuff I could make up.

events.label: A man explains how he later saw the other man at the telegraph bureau

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: He got out at Hobson's Patch, and so did I. I chanced into the telegraph bureau, and he was leaving it. He had filled the form with stuff that might have been Chinese. The clerk said he fired a sheet of this off every day. I said it was special news for his paper, and he was scared that the others should tap it.

events.label: McGinty agrees that the suspicion is right and asks what should be done

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: By Gar! I believe you are right. But what do you allow that we should do about it?

events.label: Someone suggests going at once to attack the man

communicates.speaker: unknown
communicates.content: Why not go right down now and fix him?

events.label: McMurdo says he would leave at once if he knew where to find him

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I'd start this next minute if I knew where we could find him. He's in Hobson's Patch; but I don't know the house. I've got a plan, though, if you'll only take my advice.

events.label: McMurdo describes a plan to lure the man to Widow MacNamara's house

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: I'll go to the Patch tomorrow morning. I'll find him through the operator. Then I'll tell him that I'm a Freeman myself. I'll offer him all the secrets of the lodge for a price. I'll tell him the papers are at my house, and that it's as much as my life would be worth to let him come while folk were about. Let him come at ten o'clock at night, and he shall see everything. Widow MacNamara's is a lonely house. She's as true as steel and as deaf as a post. There's only Scanlan and me in the house. If I get his promise, I'd have the whole seven of you come to me by nine o'clock. We’ll get him in. If ever he gets out alive, he can talk of Birdy Edwards's luck for the rest of his days.

events.label: McGinty agrees to wait until the next night

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: There’s going to be a vacancy at Pinkerton's or I’m mistaken. Leave it at that, McMurdo. At nine tomorrow we’ll be with you. You once get the door shut behind him, and you can leave the rest with us.

events.label: Conspirators plan to question a detective once he is in their power
McMurdo goes to Hobson’s Patch as agreed
Captain Marvin addresses McMurdo at the station

communicates.speaker: captain_marvin
communicates.content: (not specified)

events.label: McMurdo refuses to speak with Captain Marvin
McMurdo meets McGinty at the Union House and tells him that someone is coming

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: He is coming.

events.label: McGinty asks whether the man knows much

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: Do you reckon he knows much?

events.label: McMurdo answers that the man has been there about six weeks and may have passed on results

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: He’s been here some time—six weeks at the least. I guess he didn’t come into these parts to look at the prospect. If he has been working among us all that time with the railroad money at his back, I should expect that he has got results, and that he has passed them on.

events.label: McGinty proposes sending men to beat Morris and question him

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: If any man gives us away, it would be he. I’ve a mind to send a couple of the boys round before evening to give him a beating up and see what they can get from him.

events.label: McMurdo agrees that there would be no harm in that

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Well, there would be no harm in that.

events.label: McGinty declares that he will fix Morris and has watched him for a year

communicates.speaker: bodymaster_mcginty
communicates.content: I’ll fix the old devil! I’ve had my eye on him this year past.

events.label: McMurdo says the beating must wait until tomorrow and the Pinkerton affair is settled

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: But whatever you do must be to-morrow; for we must lie low until the Pinkerton affair is settled up. We can’t afford to set the police buzzing, to-day of all days.

events.label: McMurdo says Birdy Edwards will be given fake papers after he sees all of McMurdo's papers

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: I guess I took him on his weak point. If he could get on a good trail of the Scowrers, he’s ready to follow it into hell. I took his money and as much more when he has seen all my papers. What papers? Well, there are no papers. But I filled him up about constitutions and books of rules and forms of membership. He expects to get right down to the end of everything before he leaves.

events.label: McGinty says Birdy Edwards is right about wanting to get to the end of everything

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: Faith, he’s right there.

events.label: McMurdo says Captain Marvin spoke to him at the depot that day

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: As if I would carry such things, and me a suspected man, and Captain Marvin after speaking to me this very day at the depot!

events.label: McGinty says the burden of the plan is falling on McMurdo and identifies a location obstacle

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: I guess the heavy end of this business is coming on to you. We could put him down an old shaft when we’ve done with him; but however we work it we can’t get past the man living at Hobson’s Patch and you being there to-day.

events.label: McMurdo says they can prevent proof of the killing

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: If we handle it right, they can never prove the killing. No one can see him come to the house after dark, and I’ll lay to it that no one will see him go. Now see here, Councillor, I’ll show you my plan and I’ll ask you to fit the others into it. You will all come in good time. Very well. He comes at ten. He is to tap three times, and me to open the door for him. Then I’ll get behind him and shut it. He’s our man then.

events.label: McMurdo describes the next step of the ambush and the risk of shooting

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: That’s all easy and plain. Yes; but the next step wants considering. He’s a hard proposition. He’s heavily armed. I’ve fooled him proper, and yet he is likely to be on his guard. Suppose I show him right into a room with seven men in it where he expected to find me alone. There is going to be shooting, and somebody is going to be hurt. That’s so. And the noise is going to bring every damned copper in the township on top of it. I guess you are right.

events.label: McMurdo explains how he will lure Birdy Edwards into the parlour and seize his pistol arm

communicates.speaker: mcmurdo
communicates.content: This is how I should work it. You will all be in the big room—same as you saw when you had a chat with me. I’ll open the door for him, show him into the parlour beside the door, and leave him there while I get the papers. That will give me the chance of telling you how things are shaping. Then I will go back to him with some faked papers. As he is reading them I will jump for him and get my grip on his pistol arm. You’ll hear me call and in you will rush. The quicker the better; for he is as strong a man as I, and I may have more than I can manage. But I allow that I can hold him till you come.

events.label: McGinty approves the plan and says the lodge will owe McMurdo a debt

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: It’s a good plan. The lodge will owe you a debt for this. I guess when I move out of the chair I can put a name to the man that’s coming after me.

events.label: McMurdo prepares a revolver for the evening
McMurdo surveys the room prepared for the detective trap
McMurdo discusses the matter with Scanlan

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: what was intended

events.label: The men arrive for the planned killing of the Pinkerton detective
The men prime themselves with whisky
Cormac touches the stove and comments on using it

communicates.speaker: tiger_cormac
communicates.content: That will do

events.label: McMurdo remains cool while the others applaud
Boss McGinty and others wait as someone arrives at the door

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: You are the one to handle him.

events.label: McMurdo closes the curtains and leaves the room to receive the visitor
Three knocks sound at the door and McMurdo hushes the group

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Not a sound, for your lives!

events.label: The visitor is brought inside and the door is locked
McMurdo returns and reveals himself as Birdy Edwards

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: Yes, Birdy Edwards is here. I am Birdy Edwards!

events.label: Rifles appear at the windows and Boss McGinty rushes for the door

communicates.speaker: mc_murdo
communicates.content: You’re safer there, Councillor. And you, Baldwin, if you don’t take your hand off your pistol, you’ll cheat the hangman yet. Pull it out, or by the Lord that made me—There, that will do. There are forty armed men round this house, and you can figure it out for yourself what chance you have. Take their pistols, Marvin!

events.label: Birdy Edwards tells the gang he is a Pinkerton man and explains his infiltration

communicates.speaker: birdy_edwards
communicates.content: I am Birdy Edwards of Pinkerton’s. I was chosen to break up your gang. I had a hard and dangerous game to play. Only Captain Marvin here and my employers knew that. It’s over to-night, thank God, and I am the winner. Some of you will take no further hand, and there are sixty more besides yourselves that will see a jail this night. I never believed there was such a society as yours. I thought it was paper talk. I went to Chicago and was made one. I stayed to look after it. I never killed a man in Chicago. I never minted a dollar in my life. I pretended to you that the law was after me. I joined your lodge and took my share in your councils. I beat up old man Stanger the night I joined you. I held your hand, Baldwin, when you would have killed him. I could not save Dunn and Menzies. I gave Chester Wilcox warning.

events.label: McGinty hisses an accusation at Birdy Edwards

communicates.speaker: mcginty
communicates.content: You blasted traitor!

events.label: Birdy Edwards responds to McGinty and continues explaining his actions

communicates.speaker: birdy_edwards
communicates.content: You may call me that if it eases your smart. You and your like have been the enemy of God and man in these parts. It took a man to get between you and the poor devils of men and women that you held under your grip. There was just one way of doing it, and I did it. Many a thousand will call me a deliverer. I’ve had three months of it. I had to stay till I had it all, every man and every secret right here in this hand. I had to act and act quickly.

events.label: Scanlan receives a sealed note for Miss Ettie Shafter

communicates.speaker: unknown
communicates.content: Take a sealed note to the address of Miss Ettie Shafter.

events.label: A beautiful woman and a muffled man board a special train and leave the land of danger
Ettie and her lover set foot in the Valley of Fear for the last time
Ettie and her lover marry in Chicago with old Jacob Shafter as witness

The escaped men swear an oath to take Birdy Edwards's blood

communicates.speaker: ted_baldwin

events.label: Birdy Edwards is chased from Chicago after two attempts
Birdy Edwards goes under a changed name to California after leaving Chicago
Ettie Edwards dies in California
Birdy Edwards works in a lonely canyon under the name of Douglas with Barker as partner and amasses a fortune
Birdy Edwards clears for England in time
John Douglas marries a worthy mate and lives five years as a Sussex county gentleman
The police trial refers John Douglas's case to a higher court

Holmes writes to the wife to get her husband out of England at any cost

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: Get him out of England at any cost. There are forces here which may be more dangerous than those he has escaped. There is no safety for your husband in England.

events.label: An enigmatic note is slipped into the letter box
Mrs. Hudson brings up a message that a gentleman wishes to see Holmes

communicates.speaker: mrs_hudson
communicates.content: a gentleman wished to see Mr. Holmes, and the matter was of the utmost importance

events.label: Cecil Barker arrives and reports bad news to Holmes

communicates.speaker: cecil_barker
communicates.content: I’ve had bad news—terrible news, Mr. Holmes

events.label: Holmes answers that he had expected as much

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: I feared as much

events.label: Barker asks whether Holmes has had a cable

communicates.speaker: cecil_barker
communicates.content: You have not had a cable, have you?

events.label: Holmes says he has had a note from someone who has had a cable

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: I have had a note from someone who has

events.label: Barker identifies Douglas and says they started for South Africa on the Palmyra

communicates.speaker: cecil_barker
communicates.content: It’s poor Douglas. They tell me his name is Edwards; but he will always be Jack Douglas of Benito Canyon to me. I told you that they started together for South Africa in the Palmyra three weeks ago.

events.label: Barker reports that the ship reached Cape Town and reads Mrs. Douglas's cable

communicates.speaker: cecil_barker
communicates.content: The ship reached Cape Town last night. I received this cable from Mrs. Douglas this morning: Jack has been lost overboard in gale off St. Helena. No one knows how accident occurred. IVY DOUGLAS.

events.label: Holmes states that the report was stage-managed and that Jack Douglas was murdered

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: It came like that, did it? Well, I’ve no doubt it was well stage-managed. None in the world. Surely!

events.label: Barker agrees that Jack Douglas was murdered

communicates.speaker: cecil_barker
communicates.content: So I think also

events.label: Holmes rejects the Scowrers as the perpetrators and points to Moriarty

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: No, no, my good sir. There is a master hand here. It is no case of sawed-off shotguns and clumsy six-shooters. You can tell an old master by the sweep of his brush. I can tell a Moriarty when I see one. This crime is from London, not from America.

events.label: Barker asks about the motive

communicates.speaker: cecil_barker
communicates.content: But for what motive?

events.label: Holmes explains that the crime was done by a man who cannot afford to fail and that a great brain and organization were used to destroy one man

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: Because it is done by a man who cannot afford to fail, one whose whole unique position depends upon the fact that all he does must succeed. A great brain and a huge organization have been turned to the extinction of one man. It is crushing the nut with the triphammer—an absurd extravagance of energy—but the nut is very effectually crushed all the same.

events.label: Barker asks how the man came to have anything to do with it

communicates.speaker: cecil_barker
communicates.content: How came this man to have anything to do with it?

events.label: Holmes says the first word of the business came from one of Moriarty's lieutenants and describes the criminal method

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: I can only say that the first word that ever came to us of the business was from one of his lieutenants. These Americans were well advised. Having an English job to do, they took into partnership, as any foreign criminal could do, this great consultant in crime. From that moment their man was doomed. At first he would content himself by using his machinery in order to find their victim. Then he would indicate how the matter might be treated. Finally, when he read in the reports of the failure of this agent, he would step in himself with a master touch. You heard me warn this man at Birlstone Manor House that the coming danger was greater than the past. Was I right?

events.label: Barker strikes his head with his clenched fist in anger
Barker asks whether they must accept the situation

communicates.speaker: cecil_barker
communicates.content: Do not tell me that we have to sit down under this? Do you say that no one can ever get level with this king devil?

events.label: Holmes says the man can be beaten but asks for time

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: No, I don’t say that. I don’t say that he can’t be beat. But you must give me time—you must give me time!

events.label: They sit in silence for some minutes

clues.significance: Holmes inferred that Moriarty was the celebrated author of The Dynamics of an Asteroid from the reference to the book in his speech.
Holmes inferred that the cipher message referred to words in a page of some book and that Douglas and Birlstone were not contained in the page in question.
Holmes inferred that the cipher referred to a large book, likely a standardized volume printed in double columns, from the page number 534, the sign C2, and the numbered word 293.
Holmes inferred that the message was encoded in Whitaker's Almanac, then decoded the words from page 534, column two to recover the warning that danger was intended for Douglas at Birlstone House.
Holmes and Watson solved the cipher from the paper and obtained the names Douglas and Birlstone from it.
Holmes treated the letter as evidence tied to the Birlstone mystery and noted that it was posted in Camberwell.
Holmes identified the painting over the professor's head as a Jean Baptiste Greuze work and used its placement in the study as part of his examination of the room.
Holmes inferred that Moriarty was a very wealthy man from the Greuze painting and its value, and used it as evidence that the money came from an illegal source.
MacDonald reported that John Douglas had been shot in the head by a shotgun and that the case was judged to be murder with no arrest made.
Cecil Barker observed the dreadful head at the scene of the murder investigation.
Cecil Barker treated the open window and the blood smudge on the sill as evidence that someone escaped through the window after the shooting.
Sergeant Wilson treated the card as possibly left behind by the murderer and as containing initials and a number.
Dr. Wood found the hammer in the room, and Barker connected it with Douglas's picture-altering work.
Sergeant Wilson used the muddy boot marks and the drawn curtains to infer that someone had hidden in the room after four o'clock.
Dr. Wood identified the mark as a brand rather than a tattoo.
Barker inferred that the dead man's wedding ring had been removed after noticing that the nugget ring and snake ring remained while the wedding ring was gone.
White Mason found no signs of violence or stain on the hammer, so the hammer yielded no physical trace of its use.
White Mason examined the gun and found buckshot cartridges, wired triggers, a sawed-off barrel, and partial maker's lettering P-E-N.
Holmes identified the barrel marking P-E-N as Pennsylvania Small Arms Company.
White Mason treated the ring business and the card as pointing to premeditated murder for a private reason.
Holmes inferred that the window provided the relevant point of entry or exit after examining the moat edge and the open window.
Holmes inferred that the assailant dropped a card marked V.V. 341 when he escaped.
Holmes inferred that Douglas may have gripped the hammer during the struggle from its position on the mat.
Holmes examined the branded triangle inside a circle on Douglas's forearm as a significant mark in the case.
Holmes inferred that the card was not printed in the room because the ink colors and pen thickness differed from the desk supplies.
Holmes inferred that the weapon was used in the attack when he linked the gun to the blow that nearly blew Mr. Douglas's head off.
White Mason and the others found the bicycle concealed in the evergreens and treated it as a clue to the rider's movements and origin.
Cecil Barker inferred that the murderer escaped by the window from the bloodstain.
Cecil Barker ruled out drowning in the moat because it was no more than three feet deep.
Holmes inferred that Barker had stood at the window because the slipper exactly corresponded to the blood mark on the sill.
Holmes inferred that the account was impossible because the assassin would have had too little time to remove the ring, replace the other ring, and place the card beside the victim.
Holmes inferred that Barker had deliberately placed the blood mark on the windowsill to give the police a false clue.
Holmes inferred that the bicycle had been left as a blind to suggest an outsider and that the fugitive had used it for escape planning.
Holmes inferred that the stain on the windowsill supported the staged outsider theory.
Holmes inferred that the card on the body could have been prepared in the house and fit the staged explanation.
Holmes inferred that the use of a cut-off American shotgun made the guilty-couple theory harder to accept.
Holmes inferred that Barker's bloodstained slipper was used to place the mark on the windowsill to suggest how the fugitive got away.
MacDonald and White Mason identified the bicycle and used it to trace the man connected with it.
MacDonald treated the cycle map on the bedroom table as part of the physical evidence from the man who stayed in the hotel.
MacDonald used the sawed-off shotgun in the valise as evidence that Hargrave had come with the deliberate purpose of crime.
MacDonald treated the bicycle left at the scene as a clue against Hargrave.
Holmes used the repeated reports and arrests of the bicyclist to frame the investigation around the elusive rider.
Holmes used the tract about the Manor House to draw historical associations from the building's account and references to events at the house.
Holmes found the missing dumb-bell in the study and treated it as important evidence in the case.
Holmes inferred that something had been sunk in the moat from the absence of a dumb-bell and later recovered the bundle from the water.
Holmes used the missing dumb-bell to infer that the bundle had been weighted and hidden in the moat.
Holmes identified the boots as American from their toes.
Holmes presented the sheathed knife as part of the contents of the recovered bundle.
Holmes extracted a complete set of clothing from the recovered bundle.
Holmes inferred that the overcoat contained a prolonged inner pocket suitable for a truncated fowling piece and noted the tailor’s tab from Vermissa, U.S.A.
Holmes inferred that the body found in the moat was not Mr. John Douglas but the bicyclist from Tunbridge Wells from the suit of clothes found in the moat.
Watson inferred that the dead man had a lodge brand on his forearm from the mark he saw on the sleeve and forearm.
Watson inferred that the man known as Douglas had the same lodge mark on his forearm after seeing him turn up his coat and cuff.
Douglas described Barker opening the window and marking the sill to make it look as if the murderer escaped that way.
McGinty exposed a branded lodge sign on his forearm and treated it as a mark with punitive meaning.
McGinty examined the clipping and identified it as an account of the shooting of Jonas Pinto in Chicago.
McGinty inferred that the coining plant was hidden under the floor and tried to locate it before leaving.
McMurdo inferred from the letter that a detective agency had taken the matter up in dead earnest and that Pinkerton's best man, Birdy Edwards, was operating.
